title: Stonehenge Altar Stone: Origin Still a Mystery
paragraphs: Stonehenge in England has a large stone called the Altar Stone. It is a slab of sandstone, about 4.9 metres long, and it weighs about six tons. For more than a hundred years, people believed it came from Wales.

Then earlier research pointed to north-east Scotland. A new study, led by Professor Duncan Pirrie, tested this idea. The team looked at the stone at the monument and at small pieces from museum collections. They studied its structure, minerals and chemistry.
The result was surprising. None of the places they checked has the same rock as the Altar Stone. This does not prove that Scotland is wrong, but the real home of the stone is still unknown.
